title: SSC CGL 30-Day Study Plan 2026: Week-by-Week Revision Schedule
description: A 30-day SSC CGL 2026 study plan for candidates with a basic foundation: 6 hours a day, week-by-week topics, mock schedule and a final-week revision loop.
intro: A 30-day plan is a **fast revision-and-test cycle**, not a way to learn the syllabus from zero. It suits you if you have already studied school-level maths and basic English, or have attempted CGL or a similar exam before. The plan below budgets about 6 hours a day across four weeks, with mocks ramping up from week 2.

sections.title: Who this plan is for, and the daily budget
sections.body:
**Use this plan if** you can already solve basic percentage, ratio and average questions, and you can read an English passage without much difficulty. **If not, use the 60-day or 90-day plan.**

| Slot | Hours | Content |
|---|---|---|
| Quant | 2.0 | New topic (1 h) + timed practice (1 h) |
| Reasoning | 1.5 | One or two types, 30 questions |
| English | 1.5 | Grammar or vocabulary (45 min) + RC or cloze (45 min) |
| General Awareness | 1.0 | Current affairs and one static subject |
| **Total** | **6.0** | Plus 20 minutes at night for the mistakes notebook |

Working candidates: keep the same order but halve every slot (3 hours a day) and treat this as a 60-day plan. Do not compress mocks.

**Weekly rhythm.** Days 1 to 6 are study days; every 7th day (days 7, 14, 21, 28) is a test day: one mock or sectional test (1 hour), 2 hours of analysis, then re-solving mistakes. Days 29 and 30 are light revision.

sections.title: Week 1 (days 1 to 7): arithmetic, verbal reasoning, grammar
sections.body:
Goal: lock in the highest-frequency topics. Cover each with 25+ questions.

| Day | Quant (2 h) | Reasoning (1.5 h) | English (1.5 h) | GA (1 h) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Speed base (tables, squares, fractions) + [Simplification](/quant/simplification/) | [Series](/reasoning/series/) | [Grammar essentials](/english/grammar-essentials/) (tenses, agreement) | Current affairs, last 6 months |
| 2 | [Percentage](/quant/percentage/) | [Analogy](/reasoning/analogy/) | [Error spotting](/english/error-spotting/) | [Polity](/ga/polity/) |
| 3 | [Profit, Loss and Discount](/quant/profit-loss-discount/) | [Classification](/reasoning/classification/) | [Sentence improvement](/english/sentence-improvement/) | [Economy](/ga/economy/) |
| 4 | [Ratio and Proportion](/quant/ratio-proportion/) + [Average](/quant/average/) | [Coding-Decoding](/reasoning/coding-decoding/) | [Spelling](/english/spelling/) + [fill in the blanks](/english/fill-in-the-blanks/) | [Static GK](/ga/static-gk/) |
| 5 | [Number System](/quant/number-system/) + [HCF and LCM](/quant/hcf-lcm/) | [Missing number](/reasoning/missing-number/) + [mathematical operations](/reasoning/mathematical-operations/) | [Active-passive](/english/active-passive/) + [direct-indirect](/english/direct-indirect/) | Current affairs |
| 6 | Mixed arithmetic set, 40 questions timed | Mixed verbal set, 30 questions | [Cloze test](/english/cloze-test/) strategy | Revision of week GA |
| 7 | Sectional test (Quant + Reasoning), analysis | | One RC passage set | Short quiz from the [daily quiz](/daily-quiz/) |

sections.title: Week 2 (days 8 to 14): remaining arithmetic, DI, puzzles, vocabulary
sections.body:
Goal: finish arithmetic, start the big blocks, and make vocabulary a daily habit.

| Day | Quant (2 h) | Reasoning (1.5 h) | English (1.5 h) | GA (1 h) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | [Time and Work](/quant/time-work/) | [Syllogism](/reasoning/syllogism/) | [Synonyms and antonyms](/english/synonyms-antonyms/) | [Modern history](/ga/modern-history/) |
| 9 | [Time, Speed and Distance](/quant/time-speed-distance/) | [Seating arrangement](/reasoning/seating-arrangement/) | [Idioms and phrases](/english/idioms-phrases/) | [Ancient history](/ga/ancient-history/) + [medieval](/ga/medieval-history/) |
| 10 | [Interest](/quant/interest/) + [Mixture and alligation](/quant/mixture-alligation/) | [Order and ranking](/reasoning/order-ranking/) + [blood relations](/reasoning/blood-relations/) | [One-word substitution](/english/one-word-substitution/) | [Indian geography](/ga/indian-geography/) |
| 11 | [Data Interpretation](/quant/data-interpretation/) (tables, percentages) | [Direction and distance](/reasoning/direction-distance/) | [Reading comprehension](/english/reading-comprehension/) | Current affairs |
| 12 | Data Interpretation (pie, growth) | [Venn diagrams](/reasoning/venn-diagrams/) + [statement-conclusion](/reasoning/statement-conclusion/) | [Sentence rearrangement](/english/sentence-rearrangement/) | [World geography](/ga/world-geography/) |
| 13 | Arithmetic mixed set, 40 questions timed | Reasoning mixed set | Vocabulary revision (60 words) | Revision |
| 14 | **Full mock 1**, then analysis | | | |

sections.title: Week 3 (days 15 to 21): geometry, algebra, trigonometry, non-verbal, science
sections.body:
Goal: cover the advanced Quant blocks, which carry the largest question counts in shift analyses (see [weightage](/exams/ssc-cgl/weightage/)), and the figure-based reasoning types.

| Day | Quant (2 h) | Reasoning (1.5 h) | English (1.5 h) | GA (1 h) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15 | [Geometry](/quant/geometry/): lines, triangles | [Cube and dice](/reasoning/cube-dice/) | Cloze test practice | [Biology](/ga/biology/) |
| 16 | Geometry: circles, quadrilaterals | [Counting figures](/reasoning/counting-figures/) | Reading comprehension | Biology |
| 17 | [Mensuration 2D](/quant/mensuration-2d/) + [3D](/quant/mensuration-3d/) | [Mirror and water image](/reasoning/mirror-water-image/) + [paper folding](/reasoning/paper-folding-cutting/) | Error spotting mixed set | [Physics](/ga/physics/) |
| 18 | [Algebra](/quant/algebra/) | [Embedded figures](/reasoning/embedded-figures/) + [figure series](/reasoning/figure-series/) | Synonyms, idioms set | Physics |
| 19 | [Trigonometry](/quant/trigonometry/) | [Dictionary order](/reasoning/dictionary-order/) + weak types | Cloze + RC timed | [Chemistry](/ga/chemistry/) |
| 20 | [Heights and distances](/quant/heights-distances/) + [Statistics](/quant/statistics/) | Mixed set | Sentence improvement + OWS | [Art and culture](/ga/art-culture/) + current affairs |
| 21 | **Full mock 2**, then analysis | | | |

sections.title: Week 4 (days 22 to 30): mock-heavy final stretch
sections.body:
Goal: no new chapters. Convert knowledge to marks through mocks and the mistakes notebook.

| Day | Plan (6 h) |
|---|---|
| 22 | Weak-topic repair: your three lowest-accuracy Quant topics (2 h), weakest Reasoning type (1.5 h), English weak area (1.5 h), GA revision (1 h) |
| 23 | **Full mock 3** + 2 h analysis |
| 24 | Re-solve all wrong questions from mocks 1 to 3, formula sheet pass |
| 25 | **Full mock 4** + analysis |
| 26 | Vocabulary and idiom revision, current affairs of the last 3 months, static GK quick pass |
| 27 | **Full mock 5** + analysis |
| 28 | Sectional timing drill: 25 questions in 15 minutes for each section, one after another |
| 29 | Light day: formula sheet, mistakes notebook, one short quiz |
| 30 | Rest, early sleep, check the admit card details and centre |

If your mock average is stable and accuracy is above 80%, add a second mock on day 26. If it is dropping, skip a mock and use the day for error analysis instead.

sections.title: Adjusting the plan to your mock data
sections.body:
- **Quant accuracy below 70%:** extend arithmetic by two days and drop Heights and Distances for now; it is a one-question topic.
- **English below 18 out of 25:** add a 30-minute daily reading slot (an editorial or a news article) and do one cloze passage every day.
- **Running out of time in Quant:** do two 15-minute timed sets a day, and learn the shortcut for each solved question.
- **GA overload:** prioritise current affairs and Biology, which lead the shift counts, then static GK and polity.
- **Tier 2 afterwards:** once Tier 1 is over, switch to the Tier 2 strategy, since Tier 2 asks for more depth in English and Maths.

faqs.q: Can I really prepare for SSC CGL in 30 days?
faqs.a: Only as a revision cycle on top of an existing base. Learning the full syllabus from scratch in a month is unrealistic. If your basics are weak, use the 60-day or 90-day plan, and treat this one as the final month.

faqs.q: How many mocks should I take in 30 days?
faqs.a: Five full mocks and two or three sectional tests is a workable target, with at least as much time spent on analysis as on attempting. Quality of analysis matters more than count.

faqs.q: What if I am working full time?
faqs.a: Halve each daily slot to about 3 hours and stretch the schedule to 60 days. Put Reasoning and GA in short slots (commute or lunch) and keep the Quant and mock hours for focused time.

faqs.q: Which topics can I skip if I run short of time?
faqs.a: Low-frequency topics such as Mixture and Alligation, Heights and Distances, Dictionary Order and Medieval History carry 0 to 1 questions per shift. Cover them last.
No. It is built around Tier 1. After Tier 1, follow the Tier 2 guide, which adds depth in Maths and English and covers the Computer module and the data-entry speed test.
